newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen to raise petrol prices from July 1.
newsitem.headline: Yemen to raise petrol prices from July 1.

text.p: An official at Yemen's oil ministry said on Sunday the country would raise the price of petrol from July 1, a move which in the past has sparked riots and protests.

The official, who declined to be named, would not disclose the new petrol price. But the independent newspaper Al-Ayam said the price was expected to rise 30 percent to 25 rials ($0.2) per litre from a current 19 rials.
When Yemen increased the price of gasoline to 19 rials from 12 in January 1996, farmers and students took to the streets and blocked a major Sanaa-Aden highway in protest.
In 1995, riots erupted in the southern port city of Aden over the doubling of petrol prices.

Yemen, a small independent oil producer, began raising the price of gasoline in March 1995 as part of the implementation of economic reforms agreed with the World Bank and International Monetary Fund. ($1=125 rials)
